study.title: FeDETR: A Federated Approach for Stenosis Detection in Coronary Angiography

imaging.modality_detail: Coronary angiography videos; key frames extracted
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries (stenosis severity assessed against FFR/iFR)

public_dataset_used.detail: Private dataset of 1001 coronary angiographies from five hospitals

data_released.detail: Described as a private dataset; no release stated

task.task_description: Federated DETR detects the major stenosis (bounding box) in angiographic key frames and classifies it as low-severity vs mild/high-severity (hemodynamically significant by FFR<0.80 or iFR<0.89); only the backbone is federated across five hospital nodes.
task.clinical_application: Assessment of hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis to support revascularization decisions

temporal_evidence.quote: Given a key frame, the CNN backbone learns a 2D representation, which is then flattened by the model.

G2.quote: Federated learning addresses this challenge by aggregating knowledge from multiple nodes to improve model generalization

G3.quote: we aim at improving our method by automating the procedure for the selection of the key frames from angiography videos

G9.quote: the 40.5% of patients has been labeled as positive, resulting in a significant class imbalance

G10.quote: collecting and sharing large amounts of patient data distributed across multiple healthcare institutions and research centers is challenging

other_limitations: Worse bounding box localization (IoU) than baseline federated methods
Key frames selected manually by physicians
future_work: Automate key frame selection from angiography videos
